_comment: C0 body translation · presidio (2026-11-06). Key contract per cursor.en.json; sources/related counts must match the source file.

axes.model_access: It carries no generative model of its own: the Analyzer page states "Predefined recognizers leverage regex, Named Entity Recognition and other types of logic to detect PII in unstructured text." — the recognition surface combines regex, NLP (spaCy / Transformers class), rules and checksums, with context words weighting the score, and custom recognizers covered by an official tutorial. The full list of selectable NLP engines and model tiers: not itemised in this pass.
axes.runtime: Everything runs inside your own boundary: the docs home page gives the install surface as pip packages or a Docker REST API, and states that offline usage is supported with data staying inside your own deployment. No hosted service surface is offered officially (no such statement captured). Image tags and their version mapping: not verified word for word in this pass.
axes.local_files: It does not read your workspace; it processes only the text and images you explicitly hand it, and returns results inside your own process or service. Where the recognizers' language-model files are downloaded and cached, and how they are packaged offline: no word-for-word official statement captured, recorded as unknown.
axes.background: There is no hosted background task: one analyze / anonymize call is one invocation, or one pass inside your own service, with batching and retries owned by your orchestration layer. The docs table of contents (Getting Started / Analyzer / Anonymizer / Image Redactor / Samples / API Docs) contains no queue or resume concept.
axes.tools: Three API faces: AnalyzerEngine (recognition), AnonymizerEngine (transformation), Image Redactor (image masking). The operators on record from the Anonymizer page are replace, redact, hash, mask, encrypt, keep and custom, configured through OperatorConfig's type and params and combinable. MCP transport support: not described in the official docs, recorded as unknown.
axes.context: Here "context" is a literal mechanism: recognizers weight candidate entities with context words, so neighbouring words in the same text change the result; the docs home page describes the project as "fast identification and anonymization modules" for text and images. It is a stateless one-pass handler with no cross-session memory — batch context-window management belongs to your calling code.
axes.permissions: See the licence field (MIT, taken from the PyPI licence metadata; the LICENSE text was not read directly). Two measured facts about ownership: the old address microsoft.github.io/presidio displayed "This page has moved" on the verification date, and the intermediate host data-privacy-stack.github.io 301s to presidio.dataprivacystack.org, whose home page states the project is governed by Data Privacy Stack. **Data flow**: recognition and anonymisation complete inside your own deployment and offline use is supported, meaning text need not be sent to any third party. **Red line**: the Analyzer page states on record "Scores are not probabilities", so a score threshold is not a detection probability; this site publishes no detection rate, no miss rate and no product rankings. Whether it satisfies an anonymisation obligation under any given law is not a legal conclusion the project makes.
axes.fit: Fits: inserting personal-data recognition and transformation into your own pipeline (before RAG ingestion, before logs are written, before a call to a hosted model); needing operator-level composition and custom recognizers; requiring text not to leave your network boundary; needing the whole chain to run offline. Not a fit: teams wanting a hosted console and compliance deliverables; modalities beyond text and images (the surface on record stops there); anyone treating a score threshold as proof of compliance.

runs:
**This site has not run it end to end**: AnalyzerEngine/AnonymizerEngine were never installed or called, no corpus was run to test hit behaviour, so no detection rate, miss rate, precision or ranking is produced, and the number of official recognizers is not tallied. This archive only organises statements on record at the docs home page, the Analyzer and Anonymizer pages, the PyPI project page and its release history.

**Suggested measurements** (four):

- **The real cost of wiring a custom recognizer** (the tutorial is on record; the amount of change is yours to test)
- **How language models are obtained in an offline deployment** (download and cache locations are not spelled out officially)
- **Reversibility and audit trail of combined operators** (what the restore boundary looks like when replace meets encrypt)
- **Entity coverage differences outside English** (this site draws no ratio conclusion — only whether the mechanism works)
unknowns:
- The repository LICENSE text was not fetched directly (MIT recorded from the PyPI licence field)
- Item-by-item CHANGELOG.md contents, since the file body was not fetched
- The official complete list of supported languages and entity types (the recognizers docs page returned 404)
- Versions and release dates of presidio-anonymizer and presidio-image-redaction individually
- Docker image tag-to-version mapping
- Where recognizer language models are downloaded and how they are packaged offline
- The full set of selectable NLP engine tiers and version requirements
- Whether any telemetry or reporting exists (not declared by the index or docs; no counter-evidence captured)
- Mainland-network direct reachability and filing status (not measured, not searched)
related: Also "handle personal data before it reaches the model", but the difference is who executes: that archive is a hosted API with configured operators, this one runs entirely inside your own boundary.
Covers a different class of sensitive material — credentials and secrets; the two are often chained on the same pipeline, and this site does not rank them.
The orchestration side: when redaction operators must sit in an agent's input/output path, the landing point is the agent framework layer.
